sent_to_model:
I'd like help writing a review of Gianni Amelio's The Missing Star. Amelio is one of my favourite directors and Keys to the House was brilliant, so I was disappointed with this one. Please explain the maintenance man's mission in China and how his relationship with the interpreter develops. I want to discuss the places they visit, the cinematography and performances, why the relationship didn't convince me, and whether the ending felt plausible. I still admire Amelio; I want my disappointment with this film to come through alongside that.

- Tai Ling plays young interpreter Liu Hua.
- Journey locations: Baotou, Shanghai, Chongqing, Wuhan; also Yangtze River.
- Liu's son, played by Lin Wang, is introduced at her grandmother's home.
- Closed Italian steelworks sells blast furnace to China.
- Luca Bigazzi is cinematographer.
- Liu works in a Shanghai library; accepts guiding job reluctantly because pay is good.
- Gianni Amelio directed The Missing Star, adapted from bestselling novel The Dismissal.
- Three Gorges Dam displaced 1.2 million people; river communities shown await flooding when fully operational.
- Sergio Castellitto plays older maintenance manager Vincenzo Buonovolonta.
- Vincenzo discovers dangerous furnace control defect and travels to China to prevent possible fatal accident.
- Travels show poverty, crowded housing and children without adult care.
- Liu's boy abandoned by father; film presents him as hidden and unwanted under one-child policy.
- Vincenzo has no mobile phone; needs Liu's language skills.
- Earlier Italian dinner: Vincenzo's impatience with interpreting causes Liu to lose her job.
- Companions reveal past experiences and present vulnerabilities to each other.
- Vincenzo and Liu develop a friendship during their journey.
- Vincenzo and Liu's son initially meet casually; their relationship becomes central to the story.
- Pairing unconvincing; age gap a concern.
- Tai Ling: strong presence.
- Keys to the House: brilliant.
- Castellitto: talented actor.
- Photography outstanding.
- Amelio a favourite director.
- Ending implausible.
- Castellitto's performance: emotionally remote, limited expressions.
- Younger Enrico Lo Verso would have been preferable.
- China's landscapes beautiful and complex.
- Overall disappointment.
- Travel scenes engaging.

(About me: film reviewer. Length: it should come to roughly 400-800 words.)

must_cover: Explain Vincenzo's mission to find the faulty furnace equipment in China.
Describe how Vincenzo and Liu's relationship develops and why the reviewer finds it unconvincing.
Assess the Chinese locations, cinematography and performances.
Assess the ending's plausibility and express disappointment with the film compared with Keys to the House.
Convey the reviewer's continuing admiration for Amelio.
